advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the AST closure scan discover code-returning functions dynamically (or assert `targets` covers all module-level defs in _errors.py that return str literals) so a renamed/added helper cannot silently escape the vocabulary-closure check.
evidence: src/rebar/_errors.py:73 `def _workflow_caller_code`, :109 `def _llm_error_code`, :131 `def error_code_for` — the three functions returning code literals today
`assert returned, "expected to harvest at least one returned code literal"` — non-empty check is satisfied by error_code_for alone, so a missed helper is invisible
ABSENCE: no assertion that every function in _errors.py returning a str-literal is present in `targets`, so a new/renamed classifier helper drops out of coverage silently
advisory.finding: The AST closure scan hardcodes the function names to inspect (targets = {"error_code_for", "_workflow_caller_code", "_llm_error_code"}); a future helper that is renamed or newly added in _errors.py and returns a code literal is silently excluded from the scan, so the 'classifier never returns an unregistered code' guarantee can narrow without any test failure. The `assert returned` guard only proves at least one literal was harvested (from error_code_for), not that every code-emitting function was scanned.
advisory.suggested_fix: Instead of a hardcoded name allowlist, walk every module-level FunctionDef in _errors.py, or assert that the set of functions with string-literal Returns is a subset of `targets`, so a newly added code-returning helper forces an update.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Restrict the returned-code-literal harvest to the target function's own body (exclude nested function/lambda scopes) to avoid latent false positives.
evidence: `for inner in ast.walk(node): if isinstance(inner, ast.Return) and isinstance(inner.value, ast.Constant)` — descends into nested scopes indiscriminately
ABSENCE: no scope filter to restrict Returns to the target function body itself
advisory.finding: The AST scan uses ast.walk(node) over the whole function body to collect string Return constants; if any target function later gains a nested function/lambda that returns a non-code string, that string would be harvested as a 'returned code' and could trigger a spurious unregistered-code failure (or mask intent). No nested functions exist today, so this is latent.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make _returned_code_literals scan ALL functions in _errors.py (or all module/function-level Return string constants) rather than a hardcoded helper-name allowlist, so a code returned from any future helper is still covered.
evidence: src/rebar/_errors.py:159 branch 4 dispatches to `_config_coercion.ConfigError`/`InsecureUrlError` returning literals `config_unreadable`/`config_insecure_url` INLINE in error_code_for today — but the classifier design already factors branches into `_*_code` helpers, so adding another helper is a plausible refactor the scan would miss.

Litmus: the AST scan only catches drift when the new return literal lives in one of the three named functions; a return added in any other function is invisible, so the check cannot distinguish 'no unregistered codes' from 'unregistered code lives in a function I don't scan'.
advisory.finding: test_classifier_never_returns_an_unregistered_code hardcodes the set of internal helper function names it scans ({"error_code_for", "_workflow_caller_code", "_llm_error_code"}). If a future refactor adds a `return "new_code"` inside a differently-named helper (e.g. a new `_config_code`), that literal is never harvested, the `assert returned` liveness anchor is still satisfied by error_code_for's own direct literals, and the test passes — silently defeating the 'the vocabulary contract can never silently drift open' guarantee it exists to provide.
advisory.suggested_fix: Drop the `targets` name filter and walk every ast.Return with a string ast.Constant in the whole module tree (optionally restricted to functions whose name is 'error_code_for' or matches a `_*code` pattern computed from the AST, not a frozen literal set).
